chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So, last time we talked about what medicine does and today I want to take a deep dive into

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: medical data.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: And I'm going to use as examples a lot of stuff from the mimic database, which is one

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: of the databases that we're going to be using in this class.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Some of you are probably familiar with it and some of you are not.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: And there are, I hope, some take away lessons from this discussion.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So for example, a few years ago when mimic 3 was about to be released, I was playing

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: with the data and I looked at the distribution of heart rates in the care view part of the

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: database.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So mimic for those of you who don't know has intensive care data from about 60 something

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: thousand admissions to intensive care units at the Beth Israel Deakinis Medical Center

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: for a period of about 12 years.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: And one of the technical difficulties that we encountered is that in the middle of that

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: time period the hospital shifted from one information system that they used in their

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: intensive care unit to another.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Care view is the old one, the new one and of course they're not exactly compatible.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So we'll see some examples of that.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So this is the old data.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So this is from care view.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: And you look at that and say well heart rates range from 40 to 200 roughly which is okay.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: But then there's this funny thing, there are two peaks.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So where if ever do you see two peaks in physiological data?

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Not typical.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: And so my initial reaction was so that I looked a little closer and I said hmm what are

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: the heart rates look like from these two systems?

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: And if you look in care view you see the picture that I just showed you and if you look

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: in medivision you see this other picture which looks more like what you would normally

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: expect.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: And so I'm sitting there scratching my head going okay there must be some difference between

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: these.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: It's not that simultaneous with the switch over of the hospital from one information system

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: to another physiology of people changed and all of a sudden some subset of people started

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: having faster heart rates.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: But if you think about that what subset of people have faster heart rates?

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: If you're in a stress test.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Yeah kids right.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So I said hmm interesting.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So anyway if you look at the statistics you see that the mean heart rate in care view

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: is 108 and heart rate in medivision is 87.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: But of course means are not that meaningful when you look at these by-modal distributions.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So then I said well what if we just look at adults?

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So we look at people from age greater than one up to age 90 and I'll say a word about

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: that in a minute.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: But I look at those two distributions they look pretty close.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: They look pretty similar.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So that means that the number of patients of different ages in the adult group is similar

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: in the two datasets.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: But if I don't exclude the very young or the very old then I see this funny distribution

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: where I have suppressed ages greater than 90 but not the young.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: And what you see is that in care view there's this giant spike at age 0.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So what happened at the hospital is that under the old system it was also being used in

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: the NICU, the neonatal intensive care unit.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: The new system was not being used in the NICU and therefore they didn't capture data

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: about babies.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: And in fact if you look at age versus heart rate of the entire population you see two very

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: peculiar things.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So here are the adults that we've been talking about and here are the babies and sure

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: enough they have higher heart rates.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: And then here are these 300 year old people.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Go wow.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: I don't think I'm going to have a heart rate when I'm 300 years old.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So who are those people?

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Anybody have a clue?

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Yeah.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Entry errors?

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Sorry?

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Entry errors?

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: There are too many of them.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Entry errors is always a possibility but there's quite a few data points there.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Yeah.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Make me send a data but it's by that 300.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Close.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: It's not quite missing data.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So HIPAA, the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, defines a set of criteria

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: about protecting personal health information.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: And one of the things you're not allowed to do is to specify the age of somebody who

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: is 90 years old or a older.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: And the reason is because the number of 97 year olds is pretty small.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: And so if I tell you that Willie is 97 years old then you're going to be able to pick

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: him out of a population relatively easily.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: And so it's prohibited to say that.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So as a result everybody who's 90 or older gets labeled as being 300 years old in the

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: database.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: It's an artifact.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: It's like back in my youth I worked as a computer programmer at a health sciences computing

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: facility at UCLA and we used to have a convention that missing data was represented by 99999.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: And of course if you average that into a real data set you get garbage which people did regularly.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So there are problems with this and we're running into one of those.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: If you look at just the adults the two systems actually look very similar.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So the blue and red dots or the two systems and I've drawn the trend lines between them

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: and you can see that they're very similar.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So it looks like as you get older your heart rate declines very slightly but it does so

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: equally in the two data sets.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Yeah.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: I'm the previous side beyond 300 but there are people who are older than you.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Well that's because the ages there are computed at the time that the heart rate is measured.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So if you are 300 years old when you're admitted to the hospital if you stay in the hospital

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: for six months then you're 300 and a half years old by the time of that measurement.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So that's why there are data points to the right of 300.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Yeah good catch.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Okay and then this is what the babies look like and of course they do have higher heart rates.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: And here are the oldsters.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So actually there are people out to 310 years old because maybe they were discharged from

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: hospital and then at age 100 they came back.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Maybe they were 90 years old at the time they were initially admitted 10 years later they

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: came back and we recorded more data about them and so this is all relative to that 300.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Okay.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Just one example and the lesson there is be careful when you look at data because it can

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: really easily fool you because there are all kinds of funny things about the way it's

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: collected about these artifactual things like 300 year old patients and so on.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Okay.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So here's a catalog of the types of data that are available to us.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So we have typical kind of electronic health record data from hospitals, demographics,

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: age sex, socioeconomic status, insurance type language, religion, living situation, family

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: structure, location, work, etc.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: We have vital signs, your weight, your height, your pulse, respiration, rate, body temperature,

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: etc.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So these are typically the things that if you ever go to a doctor's office or you go

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: into a hospital, nurse will take you aside and weigh you and measure your height and

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: check your blood pressure and take your temperature and stuff like that.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: These are standard vital signs and so we have lots of those recorded medications, prescription

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: medications over the counter drugs, illegal drugs if you're willing not to lie to your

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: healthcare provider, alcohol.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Again, one of my earliest days I was hanging out with a cardiologist at Tufts Medical

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Center and we see this elderly lady who looks kind of terrible and we're talking to her

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: well, the doctor is talking to her, I'm trying to stay out of the way and he says, so

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: you know, do you drink alcohol and she says, oh no, never touch this stuff and then we

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: talk some more and we go out of the patient's room and the doctor turns to me out of

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: ears shot of the patient and says, oh, she's a chronic drunk and said, well, how do you

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: know?

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: And he says, well, from lab tests, from the appearance of her skin, from her general

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: demeanor, from various sort of ineffable factors and so patients lie.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: They really do because they don't want to tell you things.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Okay, medications, by the way, is a big deal so there's this whole field called MedReck,

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: medication reconciliation which is the hospitals or the doctor's offices attempt to figure

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: out what medications you're actually taking.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So I'm a member of the MIT Health Plan and if I sign into my health plan account, it

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: tells me that I'm taking some pills that I got 12 years ago as part of a laboratory

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: test.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: But we were, you know, I took two pills which were supposed to have some physiological

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: effect and then they measured that and I've never gotten another pill and never taken

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: one since then nor would it be particularly good for me but it's still on my record and

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: there's no notice of it ever having been discontinued and that's a real problem because

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: if you're taking care of a patient, you'd like to understand what drugs they're actually

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: taking and it's hard to know.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Okay, then lab tests.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So this is the things that you imagine that we do a lot of and these are components

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: of the blood and the urine mainly but also the stool saliva, spinal fluid, fluid taken

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: off, the belly joint fluid, bone marrow stuff coming out of your lungs, it's all anything

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: right?

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: And any place where you can produce some specimen they can send it to a lab and measure

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: things and they measure lots and lots of different kinds of things and these are often useful.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Pathology, qualitative and quantitative examination of anybody to shoot for example biopsy

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: samples or surgical scraps.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: You know, if they do an operation they cut something out of you that typically winds up

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: on a pathologist bench who then tries to figure out what its characteristics are and that's

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: again useful information.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Okay, microbiology, ever since pastor we know that organisms cause disease and so we're

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: quite interested in knowing what organisms are growing inside your body and typically

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: testing is not only to identify the organism but also to figure out which antibiotics

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: it's sensitive to and insensitive to and so you'll see things like reports of sensitivity

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: testing at various delusions.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: In other words they try to give a strong dose of an antibiotic, a weaker dose, a weaker

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: dose, a weaker dose, a weaker dose to see which is the minimum level of dosing that's

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: enough to kill the bacteria.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: There's a common missing there but input output of fluids is another important thing because

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: people especially in the hospital often get either dehydrated or over hydrated and neither

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: of those is good for you and so trying to keep track of what's going into and what's coming

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: out of you is important.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Then there are tons of notes so an important one that we're going to look at in this class

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: is discharge summaries so these are the typically long notes that are written at the end

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: of a hospitalization.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So this is a summary of why you came in, what they did to you, the main things they discovered

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: about you and then plans for what to do after you discharge, where are you going to go,

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: what drugs are you going to be taking, when are you supposed to come back for follow-up

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: etc.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: I'll show you an excruciatingly long one of those later in the lecture today but we also

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: have notes from attendings that were residents, nurses, various specialties, consultants, the

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: referring physician.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: If somebody sends you to the hospital that doctor will usually write a note saying this

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: is what I'm interested in, here's why I'm sending in the patient.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: There are letters back to the referring physician saying okay this is what we found out, here's

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: the answer to the question you were asking.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: There are emergency department notes so that's often the first contact between the patient

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: and the healthcare system.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So these are all important and then there's tons and tons of billing data.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So remember the EHR systems were initially designed by accountants and they were designed

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: for the purpose of billing and so we capture a lot of data about formalized ways of describing

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: the condition of the patient and what was done to the patient in order to submit the

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: right bills.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: You obviously want a bill for as much as possible but you have to be able to justify the bills

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: that you submit because insurance companies and Medicare and Medicaid don't have a good

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: sense of humor and if you submit bills for things that you can't justify then you get penalized.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Okay.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: And then there are administrative data like which service are you on?

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So this is occasionally a confusing thing.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: You can go into the hospital and have heart problems but it turns out that the heart intensive

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: care unit, the cardiac intensive care unit is full up with patients but there's an extra

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: bad in the pulmonary intensive care unit and so they stick you in that unit but you're

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: still on the cardiology service and so there are these sort of mixture kinds of cases that

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: you still have to take care of.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Transfers are when you get transferred from one place to another in the hospital.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Imaging data.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So I'm not going to talk about that much today but there are x-rays ultrasound, CT, MRI,

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: PET scans, retinal scans andoscopy, photographs of like your skin and stuff like that.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So this is all imaging data and there's been a tremendous amount of progress recently

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: in applying machine learning techniques to try to interpret the contents of these data

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: so these are also very important.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: And then there's the whole quantified self movement.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: I mean how many of you wear an activity tracker?

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: Only about a third.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: I'm surprised that the place like MIT.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: So you know we measure steps in elevation change and workouts and you can record vital

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: signs and diet and your blood sugar especially if you're diabetic, allergies, allergic incidents.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: There's all this mindfulness, mood, sleep, pain, sexual activity and then people have

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: developed this idea of end-of-one experiments where for example I had a student some years

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: ago who was suffered from psoriasis.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: It's a proteic condition of the skin and the problem is there are no good cures for

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: it and so people who suffer from psoriasis try all kinds of things.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: You know they stop eating nuts for a while or they dust themselves with vinegar or they

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: do whatever crazy thing comes to mind.

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: And we don't have a good theory for how to treat this disease but on the other hand some

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: things work for some people and so there's a whole methodology that has been developed

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
chunks.text: that says when you try these things act like a scientist, have hypotheses, take good

chunks.title: ML_for_health_high_res
